subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Encoders: Knowing Where You Are
description: Learn Encoders: Knowing Where You Are in one minute.

hook.text: A robot needs to know the exact angle of every joint at all times. Encoders provide that knowledge.

buildup.text: Incremental encoders count pulses as the shaft turns. More pulses per revolution means finer resolution.

discovery.text: Absolute encoders know their exact position even after power loss. They never need a home run on startup.

twist.text: A robot with a million-count encoder resolves positions to 0.001 degrees. That's less than a human hair's width at the tool tip.

climax.text: Without encoders, a robot is blind. Every motion command depends on knowing the current joint positions precisely.

punchline.text: Count the ticks. Know your angle. Move with confidence.

quiz.question: What advantage do absolute encoders have over incremental ones?
options: They provide higher resolution at lower cost than incremental encoders
They know their exact position even after a power loss without re-homing
They measure speed more accurately than incremental encoders
